extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of psychology, philosophy, and humor theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and evaluating theoretical criteria for laughter and humor from a historical/psychological survey (Darwin, Freud, Lipps, Joubert, Hecker, German aestheticists). Useful for assessing adequacy of accounts of humor and laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter as expression of mere joy or happiness (Darwin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter 'seems primarily to be the expression of mere joy or happiness.' Examples: children at play, meeting an old friend, trivial pleasures; a graduated series from violent laughter to gentle smile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Darwin's observations: meaningless laughter in high spirits, laughter as part of joyful meetings between parents and offspring and among social community members; theory should account for laughter as an expression of general pleasure/satisfaction and its gradations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter as fulfillment of the social/gregarious instinct
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter is an act — a fulfilment in its own proper degree of the social instinct; to exchange a smile or laugh is to do something social and participatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This locates the origin/function of laughter in companionship and friendly meeting (vocalizations as calls or charms); a satisfactory theory should connect laughter to social interaction and the mutual reinforcement of smiling/laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of psychic expenditure (Freud)
rubrics_metrics.description: Freud's proposal that pleasurable effects in play, wit, and humor originate from the 'unexpected economy of psychic expenditure' — saved or economized psychic energy produces pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied by Freud to children's word-play, jests, wit, and humor; theory-users should show how repetition, rediscovery, or sound-association can be sources of economy and thus pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation/compression in wit (Freudian account of wit technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: In witticisms some 'condensation' occurs so that 'a given amount of verbal or conceptual effort conveys more than its usual amount of meaning' — a compressing or economizing technic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freud analyzes many witticisms as employing condensation; a theory should identify and explain mechanisms by which linguistic or conceptual compression yields wit (and be able to handle counterexamples where the effort seems greater than a direct statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendency wit: pleasure from release of inhibited energy (Freud)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 'tendency wit' Freud sometimes argues that pleasure arises not from fulfilment of the tendency itself but from the fact that 'the energy which had been employed in preventing its fulfilment is released.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Freud's attempt to reconcile wit-as-gratification and wit-as-economy; an adequate theory should coherently account for both gratification and the role of inhibition/release of psychic energy without contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor as relief at overprepared feeling / economy of feeling (Lipps/Spencer via Freud)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor arises when a prepared emotion (sympathy, anger, pain, compassion, etc.) proves excessive or uncalled for upon the event's arrival, and the soul is 'relieved at the sudden saving of passion' producing laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freud calls this an 'economy of expenditure in feeling.' Theories should explain how expectation/overpreparation of emotion and relief at its nonrealization produce the distinctive parsimony-pleasure of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for the comic emotion distinct from mere pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: A theory must explain the 'comic emotion' — the qualitative feeling specific to humor — which Freud fails to perceive: jokes that release impulses give rise to a comic emotion that dreams (even when interpreted) do not produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theoretical accounts should distinguish mere pleasure (e.g., pleasure in nonsense) from the additional 'comic' quality and explain why certain releases produce laughter with a comic feeling while others (e.g., dream interpretation) do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental criterion: children’s pleasure in nonsense vs adult humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Children enjoy 'pure pleasure in nonsense' and are described as 'without humor' in Freud's account; adult humor, by contrast, requires nonsense combined with sense. A good theory must explain this developmental change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theory should account for why children take pleasure in nonsense alone, how maturity introduces serious meanings that 'flavor' adult humor, and why nonsense becomes comic for adults only when combined with sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-mixture/contrast theory (Joubert, Mendelssohn, Lessing et al.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor as a 'contrast' or 'mixture' of desirable and undesirable qualities (e.g., perfection with imperfection): laughable arises from incongruity or contrast that is not too strong and admits blending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical variants require the contrast to be 'of no weight' or 'not too sharp'; a theory using this rubric must specify the allowable degree/kind of contrast and how blending or partial assimilation produces comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor as mixture of pleasure and pain; rhythmic alternation (Joubert, Hecker)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joubert: laughter arises when heart experiences quickly mixed joy and sadness (pleasure exceeding sadness). Hecker: comic feeling consists of 'a rapid oscillation back and forth between pleasure and pain' of approximately equal strength producing intermittent joyful surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These scientific/physiological accounts attempt to link peripheral stimulation, sympathetic nervous activity, pupil dilation, blood-pressure changes, and diaphragm action to laughter; adequate theories should address physiological correlates and explain limitations (e.g., tickling is peculiar; oscillation analogy may be fragile).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain tickling and its connection to laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: Any true science of humor 'must carry with it the explanation of our pleasure in tickling' — tickling produces a light pain and a false pleasure and causes diaphragm shaking analogous to laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theories should explain why tickling sometimes induces laughter, how peripheral nerve stimulation and sympathetic responses relate to laughter, and why tickling-laughter differs from other laughter types (mood/condition dependence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychic damming / enhancement of the sublime (Lipps)
rubrics_metrics.description: When prepared for the sublime and encountering something small, 'psychic damming' leaves energy ready to value a truly sublime thing later; humor's mission is 'to make the sublime appear lovable' and to seek sublimity in the concealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theoretical accounts should explain how contrast can increase appreciation of the sublime and how humor functions aesthetically to revalue or reveal deeper qualities in what first appears trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ridiculousness as ugliness/unseemliness (Aristotelian root)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ludicrous is 'always an ugly or unseemly object'; derisive feeling about such objects is often mixed with pain, and the combination contributes to laughability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A theory should specify the role of perceived ugliness/unseemliness in provoking derisive amusement and how that element interacts with other factors (contrast, relief, social context) to produce laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical adequacy: alignment with Darwinian observations
rubrics_metrics.description: We should 'distrust any theory of humor' that does not accord with Darwin's rediscovery that men laugh when happy and that vocal sounds are associated with joyful meetings; theories ought to find themselves in accord with evolutionary/social observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Darwinian evidence (comparative observation, social calls/charms, parent-offspring interactions) as a baseline constraint: satisfactory theories must accommodate laughter's social, evolutionary, and expressive dimensions.
